resources.string: A quick tour of what this version brought, slide by slide. It shows once by itself after an update; A shows it again.
After an update to a new version, the tour of what it brought opens once by itself. Off, it never does; the row above still shows it.
This version and new ones: check, update, and see what each brought.
After the update, Pip shows you around what\'s new.
Y on a tile lifts it right where it sits, with Open and Edit. Hold Y to pick it up and move it. On an empty spot, Y brings New, Sort and Search.
Edit is one screen now: Look, Options and Organize, with a live preview. Upload your own icon, hero or logo (GIFs move!) and round each tile\'s corners just so.
Start › Layout puts each layout on your real home. L1 and R1 flip through them, A keeps one, B puts everything back.
A new layout: a page per system or collection, the game\'s art filling the screen behind its row. L1 and R1 slide from page to page.
L1 and R1 jump between groups on every layout, with a strip showing where you land. The highlight glides from icon to icon, and the Continue card leads the way.
Fetch real console photos and logos, or dress every system in one of four art sets drawn by Tandem: Pastel Pop, Neon Arcade, Paper Cartridge or Minimal Mono.
Games from DroidDeck (every store) and GameNative turn up on their own, one tile each. Needs root until those apps share their library.
Share it, hear it, feel it
Send your look as a file, a link or a QR code, or grab one from the community gallery. Then try Thock\'s deep keyboard sounds and a light buzz on every move.
Every Monday, a board of games from your own shelves, each with its reason: pick up where you left off, almost there, short tonight. X re-rolls a row, Y says Not for me.
Select spins a reel of covers that lands on something to play, from this week\'s picks first. Any button stops the reel.
A game on several discs is one tile now. Your emulator wants an .m3u? Settings › Library & art writes one beside the discs.
Names sort without “The”, favourites can come first, and smart folders learn rating, developer, publisher, play time and last played, with All or Any.
Press Up in search for system, genre, year, rating, status, played and favourites. Type nothing and they browse your whole library.
A RetroAchievements game\'s whole list, with filters, sorts and players\' hints, on the other screen while you play too. Disc games now match by their hash.
Settings opens on eight tiles, each with a tiny live sketch of what\'s inside. Something odd? Send a bug report saves one for you, no computer needed.
Fresh music to browse by, soft and warm, like a blanket for your library. Turn it up in Settings › Sound & music.
Pass another Tandem and you swap cards: your character, a greeting, a favourite game. Bluetooth only, and off until you turn it on in Settings › Play & system › Bump.
Everyone you bump into ends up in a little town square. They stroll, chat, sit on the benches and wave. Wave back, and they get it the next time you meet.
Me is where you make your character: face, eyes, hairstyles, hats, outfits and more, all redrawn friendlier. Stuck? X picks something at random, Y takes it back.
Plaza, Lagoon and Terrace replace the old soundtracks: easy background grooves on marimba, kalimba and plucked strings, made right in Tandem. Pick one in Settings › Sound & music.
The Settings home has roomier tiles, three to a row, and every setting has a little icon of its own, so you spot it at a glance.
A game built in both Peanuts apps now plays in the official Peanuts Native, the one kept up to date. Your save from the other one comes along.
Re-roll a row in This week and the highlight stays where it was. Highlights no longer get cut off at the edges, and a crash in fitted text is gone.
